A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same unlearning evaluation framework, advantage metric and SWAP test. The complete 20-page v2 and 22-page v3, including appendices, provide readable text, equations, figures and tables supporting reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 Section 4 reports original CIFAR10 experiments, including DP-budget comparisons, dataset-size and random-seed studies, and SWAP-versus-random-split variance measurements.

after.justification: v3 Section 4 and Appendix C report original image-classification experiments, additional dataset and sensitivity evaluations, and certified linear-unlearning results.

M1.justification: The advantage and Unlearning Quality metrics, paired forget/test-set swapping, weak-adversary restriction and practical supremum approximation remain unchanged. Renaming the defender as challenger and LEARN/UNLEARN as LR/UL, and expanding their explanations, do not introduce a different method.

E1.justification: v2 evaluates CIFAR10 image classification. v3 adds CIFAR100 and MNIST classification in Appendix C.4, plus a distinct MNIST digits 3-versus-8 binary classification task for certified linear unlearning. These substantially broaden the evaluated data and task coverage.

E2.justification: v3 adds SALUN and SSD to the unlearning-method comparisons in the DP-budget tables, expanding the six-method set in v2 to eight. It also evaluates Guo et al.'s certified linear-unlearning algorithm with retraining as a reference. The comparator evaluation metrics, IC score and 1 minus MIA AUC, remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The stated DP-training budget changes from 100 epochs in v2 Section 4.1 to 20 in v3 Appendix C.2; the PDFs do not establish whether experiments were rerun. The dataset-size study changes alpha from 0.25 to 0.1. Added protocols include unlearning-fraction and model-depth sweeps, full-data/augmentation controls, and linear certified-removal testing with delta = 10^-4.

E4.justification: v3 adds sensitivity studies over unlearning fractions and ResNet architectures, plus an ablation examining training-data size and augmentation as explanations for low accuracy. The dataset-size analysis is revised. Conversely, v2 Figure 2(B)'s random-seed study and Table 2's direct SWAP-versus-random-split variance comparison are removed, rather than relocated.

E5.justification: v3 adds standard-error threshold annotations below 0.01 and 0.005 to the DP tables and reports means with standard deviations in Table 4. Both versions retain the three-model averaging statement, while v2's explicit four-seed variance comparison disappears. These changes extend uncertainty disclosure without establishing an increase in repeated runs.

E6.justification: The shared Q, IC and MIA DP-table entries remain numerically identical despite the changed stated training budget. v3 adds substantial results, including SSD and SALUN Q scores of 0.888 and 0.689 at infinite epsilon, and the coverage and sensitivity results in Tables 4–8. Dataset-size results are replaced under different alpha, while the earlier seed and SWAP-versus-random variance results are removed.

T1.justification: v3 Appendix B.5 adds a six-point counterexample and Claim B.6 with a proof showing how offset MIA accuracy can fail to distinguish unlearning methods. The principal definitions, grounding theorem, certified-removal bound and proof arguments are retained. The separately stated SWAP-grounding proposition makes an existing consequence explicit.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims: an advantage-based evaluation metric, grounding at retraining, a connection to certified removal, and efficient SWAP approximation. The cryptographic title and framing clarify an already stated foundation; the additional experiments support retained contributions.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations for low model accuracy and large DP budgets, practical motivation for adversaries exploiting shared membership across groups, and an interpretation of dataset difficulty. The weak-MIA limitation moves to Remark 4.1, but v2's explicit limitation to one round of unlearning disappears.

D1.justification: v3 Appendix C.1 newly identifies the Xeon Gold 6338 CPU, four NVIDIA A40 GPUs and approximate experiment durations. It also discloses the omission of augmentation in the main setup. Most optimizer and training details are retained and moved to Appendix C.2, with the DP epoch count substantively revised.

R1.justification: v3 adds references to Katz and Lindell, Dwork, SALUN, SSD and MNIST, and explicitly explains its connection to cryptographic security games. Most related-work discussion is retained through relocation to Appendix A. Removing the duplicate Carlini preprint entry does not remove that work, whose published version remains cited.

P1.justification: v3 substantially reorganizes and condenses the main narrative: it introduces cryptographic preliminaries, rewrites the framework exposition, shortens related work, and moves proof and experimental details into reorganized appendices. Terminology and the title change throughout, and the broader-impacts appendix is removed.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn and relabeled, while the two-panel Figure 2 is removed. The IC and MIA tables become panels of v3 Table 2, accuracy rows move into a separate appendix table, and dataset-size results receive a replacement tabular display. New Tables 5–8 and changed table placement substantially revise the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens empirical support beyond v2's CIFAR10 evaluation through additional datasets, newer unlearning methods and direct certified linear-unlearning experiments. Uncertainty reporting and explanations of low accuracy also improve assessability. These gains are tempered by removal of the seed and SWAP-versus-random evidence despite retaining the seed-robustness claim, and by the unexplained 100-to-20-epoch DP-training revision with unchanged shared scores.
